# Sections

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/Sections.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/Sections.hpp`.

A row of large text headers over the selected item's content.

An optional title sits above the header row, and optional left/right header elements flank it. When the headers do not all fit, they form a carousel by default. The selected header leads the row and the rest follow it, wrapping around. Only then do the keyboard and the navigation buttons shown on hover wrap too. The selected header is underlined with an accent bar. A change of selection flies the old content out and the new one in from the side the selection moved to. The header row is the tab stop. Left/Right select the previous/next item and Home/End the first/last. Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp step the selection from anywhere inside. [`ui::Sections`](#uisections) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::Sections{
    .title      = std::string{"EMAIL"},
    .min_height = 400.0f,
    .on_selection_changed = [](std::size_t index) { /* e.g. mark items read */ },
    .items = {
        ui::Section{.header = "All",     .content = ui::Text{.text = "all emails go here."}},
        ui::Section{.header = "Unread",  .content = ui::Text{.text = "unread emails go here."}},
        ui::Section{.header = "Flagged", .content = ui::Text{.text = "flagged emails go here."}},
    },
});

// Imperatively:
auto sections = std::make_unique<ui::SectionsControl>();
sections->set_title("EMAIL");
ui::TextControl* all = sections->add_item("All", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("all emails"));
sections->add_item("Unread", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("unread emails"));
sections->on_selection_changed([](std::size_t index) { /* ... */ });
sections->set_selected_index(1);
```

## `ui::Sections`

Large text headers over swappable content. Builds a [ui::SectionsControl](#uisectionscontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::size_t> current_folder{0};
window.set_content(ui::Sections{
    .title                = "EMAIL",
    .on_selection_changed = [&](std::size_t i) { current_folder = i; },
    .items                = {
        ui::Section{ .header = "All", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "all emails go here." } },
        ui::Section{ .header = "Unread", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "unread emails go here." } },
        ui::Section{ .header = "Flagged", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "flagged emails go here." } },
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Sections{
    .title, .selected_index, .header_carousel_enabled, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_selection_changed,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .items, .left_header_content, .right_header_content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uisections-title"></span>`title` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The small caption above the headers; empty draws none. |
| <span id="uisections-selected_index"></span>`selected_index` | `ui::TwoWayField<std::size_t>` | `{0}` | The selected item; clamped to the items. |
| <span id="uisections-header_carousel_enabled"></span>`header_carousel_enabled` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{true}` | Headers that do not fit rotate so the selected one leads. False scrolls the row instead. |
| <span id="uisections-on_selection_changed"></span>`on_selection_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(std::size_t)>` |  | Called with the new index whenever the selection moves. A bound value doesn't run it. |
| <span id="uisections-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uisections-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uisections-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uisections-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uisections-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uisections-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uisections-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Sections>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uisections-items"></span>`items` | `ui::SectionList` |  | The items, in header order. |
| <span id="uisections-left_header_content"></span>`left_header_content` | `ui::Spec` |  | An element left of the headers. |
| <span id="uisections-right_header_content"></span>`right_header_content` | `ui::Spec` |  | An element right of the headers. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `enabled`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

## `ui::SectionList`

A built, owned list of [Sections](#uisections) items. Callers never name it, since a braced list of [`ui::Section{...}`](#uisection) converts to it.

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp

    .entries
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |

| <span id="uisectionlist-entries"></span>`entries` | `std::vector<Entry>` |  | The items, in header order. |

## `ui::SectionsControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ValueProvider`.

A row of large text headers over the selected item's content.

An optional title sits above the header row, and optional left/right header elements flank it. When the headers do not all fit, they form a carousel by default. The selected header leads the row and the rest follow it, wrapping around. Only then do the keyboard and the navigation buttons shown on hover wrap too. The selected header is underlined with an accent bar. A change of selection flies the old content out and the new one in from the side the selection moved to. The header row is the tab stop. Left/Right select the previous/next item and Home/End the first/last. Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp step the selection from anywhere inside. [`ui::Sections`](#uisections) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::Sections{
    .title      = std::string{"EMAIL"},
    .min_height = 400.0f,
    .on_selection_changed = [](std::size_t index) { /* e.g. mark items read */ },
    .items = {
        ui::Section{.header = "All",     .content = ui::Text{.text = "all emails go here."}},
        ui::Section{.header = "Unread",  .content = ui::Text{.text = "unread emails go here."}},
        ui::Section{.header = "Flagged", .content = ui::Text{.text = "flagged emails go here."}},

// Imperatively:
```

### add_item

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add_item(std::string header, std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

Appends an item, taking ownership of its content, and returns a non-owning observer to the content. The first item added becomes selected.

### add_item

```cpp
void add_item(SectionsControlItem item)
```

Appends `item`, taking ownership of its content (which may be null for a header-only item). The first item added becomes selected.

The header text of item `index`; an empty string when out of range.


The title above the header row; empty collapses the title row.


```cpp

```

The selected item; unset while there are no items.

### set_selected_index

```cpp
void set_selected_index(std::size_t index)
```

Selects item `index`, clamped to the items. Does nothing, and fires nothing, if the item is already selected.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(std::size_t)> handler)
```

Fired with the new index whenever the selection changes, by click, keyboard, the navigation buttons or [`set_selected_index()`](#set_selected_index). Replaces any previous handler.

### header_carousel_enabled

```cpp
bool header_carousel_enabled() const
```

Whether the headers form a carousel, true by default. Headers that do not fit then rotate so the selected one leads. False keeps them in order and scrolls the row to the selection.

### set_header_carousel_enabled

```cpp
void set_header_carousel_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Updates the layout and redraws.

An element left of the headers. Takes ownership (replacing any previous one) and returns a non-owning observer.

### for_each_child


Lists the left header, the right header and the selected item's content. An unselected item's content is set aside, and nothing reaches it until it is selected again.

Exposed to accessibility tools as a tab control whose value is the selected header.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A click on a header selects it, and a click on a navigation button moves by one. Other input goes to the selected content.

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Also clears the content still flying out after a selection change.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the selection-change fly-in/fade animation.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Left/Right select the previous/next item, Home/End the first/last.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme&) const override
```

Around the header row, square.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme&) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.
